10 Two balls X and Y are moving towards each other with speeds of 5 m s–1 and 15 m s–1
respectively.
5 m s–1
15 m s–1
X
Y
They make a perfectly elastic head-on collision and ball Y moves to the right with a speed
of 7 m s–1.
What is the speed and direction of ball X after the collision?
A
3 m s–1 to the left
B
13 m s–1 to the left
C
3 m s–1 to the right
D
13 m s–1 to the right

hints: Notice the initial speeds $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right for X and $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the left for Y, so their speed of approach is the sum.
Recall that for a perfectly elastic head-on collision the relative speed of separation equals the relative speed of approach along the line of impact.
Use Y moving right at $7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ after impact to set separation speed equal to $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and solve for the velocity of X, taking right as positive.
walkthrough: Take right as positive. Then $u_X = +5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $u_Y = -15\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and after collision $v_Y = +7\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
For a perfectly elastic collision, relative speed is conserved: speed of approach = speed of separation.
Speed of approach $= u_X - u_Y$ in magnitude $= 5 - (-15) = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Let $v_X$ be the final velocity of X. Speed of separation $= |v_Y - v_X| = |7 - v_X|$. Set it equal to $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Since Y rebounds to the right, X must rebound to the left for head-on separation, so $7 - v_X = 20$.
Hence $v_X = 7 - 20 = -13\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which is $13\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the left. This is option B.

A.explanation: A speed of $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the left would give a separation speed of only $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, not equal to the $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ approach speed.

B.explanation: A velocity of $-13\text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives separation speed $7 - (-13) = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, equal to the approach speed for a perfectly elastic collision.

C.explanation: Motion of X to the right at $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ would give separation speed of only $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from Y moving right at $7\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Motion of X to the right at $13\text{ m s}^{-1}$ would give a separation speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, far less than the required $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
